thread:
melissa: Heads-up — P95 latency in eu-dedicated1 jumped from ~60ms -> ~420ms around 08:14 UTC. Slot saturation + KV evictions visible. Tagging @sasha @henry @raj.
raj: Oncall? Can you take a look pls.
sasha: Looking now — preliminary traces show a lot of kernel fallback to generic paths and small batch sizes. Could be noisy tenant + placement skew.
melissa: Placement dashboard: pool eu-dedicated1-1 has 85% slots used, and three tenants with 'affinity: high' pinned to same host group.
henry: Eviction logs for host-gpu-44: eviction_rate=12k/s, cpu=98%, gpu_util=97%. KV cache churn is crazy — TTL churn and repeated misses.
sasha: Pulled perf samples from 08:10-08:20, aggregated kernel profile:
```
top kernels (08:10-08:20):
  matmul_optimized       45%  (expected)
  generic_matmul         32%  (fallback, slow)
  kv_lookup              15%
  batch_pack             8%
```
melissa: Why is generic_matmul at 32%? Kernel-selection should pick matmul_optimized for seq_len <512.
sasha: Noticed seq_len distribution shifted (more long seqs + many tiny batches due to fragmentation). Also a recent runtime tweak (PR #4321) changed the selector's cost weights — suspect regression.
raj: If PR #4321 is the culprit can we rollback? What's the blast radius?
sasha: We can patch selector to short-circuit: force matmul_optimized when batch_size >=4 and median_seq_len <=256. That’s a quick canary we can push to eu-dedicated1 in ~10m.
deploy-bot: deploy: started canary deploy runtime-patch/sel-fix -> eu-dedicated1 (canary) by sasha at 2267800140
melissa: Also, placement controller logs show it ignored a spread constraint after a quota bump for tenantA — it left many small shards pinned instead of rebalancing. Possibly a bug in the affinity->spread fallback path.
henry: I can temporarily change tenantA affinity to 'balanced' and trigger drain of small slots to spread load. This will cause evictions but should reduce host pressure. Approve?
melissa: Approved. Prefer non-disruptive: drain small slots with move_tenants script, no full host evac if possible.
henry: Doing change now.
opsbot: quota_change: tenantA affinity updated by henry (high -> balanced) at 2267800150
sasha: After kernel selector patch (canary) P95 dropped from ~420ms -> ~180ms. Still seeing KV eviction high and cache_hit_rate low.
melissa: What are current cache stats?
henry: Host-level cache_hit_rate=0.27, tenantA cache_quota=64MB. Many prefixes are short-lived and churned out. Suggest bumping tenantA cache_quota to 192MB as temporary mitigation.
melissa: Go ahead with temporary bump.
opsbot: quota_change: tenantA cache_quota updated by henry (64MB -> 192MB) at 2267800158
melissa: After quota bump and selector patch, observed P95 ~95ms and throughput restored. CPU/gpu stabilized on previously hot hosts.
raj: Nice. Root causes: (1) placement/affinity bug left noisy tenant concentrated -> hot hosts, (2) kernel-selection weight regression from PR #4321 causing fallbacks when batches fragmented, (3) KV cache quota too small for the tenant's access pattern, causing eviction thrash.
sasha: Action items I’ll take: open runtime PR to revert/adjust selector weights + add canary rule (generic_matmul >20% alert), add a perf regression test with seq_len/batch distribution to catch this.
henry: I'll add placement controller fix PR (ensure spread constraint honored after quota updates), and add an integration test that simulates affinity bumps. Also add per-tenant cache quota autoscaling heuristics doc.
melissa: Ops follow-ups: add incident runbook section for "kernel fallback spike" and a dashboard tile showing generic_matmul ratio + kv_eviction_rate.
raj: Also recommend adding an automated mitigation: if host_gpu_util>90% and eviction_rate>5k/s, auto-shift noisy tenants by lowering affinity and increasing their cache_quota temporarily.
sasha: I'll attach profiling artifacts and a mini repro script in the runtime PR.
melissa: Filing the incident report and tagging customer success for any affected tenants. Thanks everyone.
opsbot: incident created INC-2026-078, severity: P2 at 2267800178
